meta.description: Strong candidate solves Two Sum with a hash-map approach on the first pass; no hints requested.

events.question_text: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution; you may not use the same element twice.

optimal_approaches.name: hash_map
key_steps: For each element, check if (target - element) is in the map

brute_force_approach.name: nested_loops
key_steps: For each i, for each j > i, check if nums[i]+nums[j]==target

events.text: Walk me through how you'd approach this problem.

I would use a hash map. As I iterate through the array, for each element I check whether the complement, which is target minus the current value, has already been stored. If it has, I return the two indices. Otherwise I store the current value mapped to its index. That gives O of n time and O of n space.
Sounds reasonable. What's the worst-case complexity, and can you handle duplicates?

Worst case is O of n because we visit every element once and each hash map operation is O of one on average. Duplicates work because I check the map before inserting, so if target is twice the current value and we've already seen it, we get a valid pair.
